author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing shape holds with one small adjustment. Both surfaces stay Web controllers adapting one HTTP surface, and the filter is a derived finder on the existing VetRepository (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller and Repository rows). No new package, type family, or layer. The durable-memory delta is written this dispatch: system-design.md § Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository and VetController now carry REQ-VET-003; § Persistence records that the specialty-filtered reads stay outside the vets cache and that case folding happens in the query rather than in column collation; the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable vet route serves no requirement is removed, since REQ-VET-003 makes it a supported surface. Resolution basis: full reads of VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, Vets.java and vets/vetList.html, not grep. The IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so no symbol-resolution citation is available.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList takes an optional specialty request parameter; the controller strips it, treats blank as absent, and chooses between the unfiltered and filtered paged finder
VetController.showResourcesVetList takes the same parameter and fills the existing Vets wrapper from the filtered or unfiltered collection finder

VetRepository gains two derived finders restricting on the joined specialty name ignoring case — one paged for the HTML surface, one unpaged for the machine-readable surface; neither is annotated @Cacheable
vets/vetList.html paging links carry the active specialty; the model attribute is null when no filter is active

patterns.description: processFindForm strips the search term, treats the absent case as the broadest listing, then delegates to a paged derived finder. The specialty parameter follows this shape; the PRD's padded-name reading is the same strip

findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) — the derived-finder shape for the new specialty finders; explicit underscore traversal (findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase) names the property path unambiguously and the project's Checkstyle carries only the NoHttp check, so the underscore passes
addPaginationModel and findPaginated — the page-size and model-attribute seam the filter threads through; the page size stays the local variable it is today
the new finders carry no caching annotation; only the two whole-directory reads stay cached

risks.risk: A paging link built by string concatenation, as vetList.html builds them today with the @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} idiom, would emit the caller-supplied specialty into the href unencoded. A name containing & or # or + breaks the link and drops or corrupts the filter.
risks.mitigation: Build every vetList.html paging link with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters — @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} — which URL-encodes each value. The engine's default output escaping stays on (security-principles.md § Realization, cross-site scripting row).

risks.risk: An unfiltered request must render exactly as today (PRD REQ-VET-003: without the parameter both surfaces behave exactly as they do today). An empty-string model attribute would leak a bare specialty= into every paging link.
risks.mitigation: Put the normalized specialty in the model as null when absent or blank. Thymeleaf omits a null link parameter, so unfiltered links keep their current form.

risks.risk: Annotating the new finders Cacheable on the vets cache would key an unbounded, never-evicted cache on caller-supplied text, so request volume alone grows heap. The vets cache has no size limit (system-design.md § Contracts, CacheConfiguration row; § Open Questions from the Survey item 5).
risks.mitigation: The two new finders carry no caching annotation (docs/adr/2026-09-06-vet-cache-excludes-filtered-reads.md; system-design.md § Persistence).

risks.risk: Reviewers read new controller code against the Web controller row, which admits no business rule and states that a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog).
risks.mitigation: Keep the controller's addition to request adaptation: strip the parameter, treat blank as absent, select the finder. The matching semantics — whole name, case-insensitive — live in the derived query, not in the controller.

risks.risk: A query that fetch-joins the EAGER specialties collection under a Pageable pages in memory rather than in the database.
risks.mitigation: Use a plain derived finder that restricts on the joined name without fetch-joining it; system-design.md § Persistence records that paging stays in the database.

risks.risk: Matching by column collation would repeat the owner-search divergence, where the same search returns different results per vendor (system-design.md § Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: IgnoreCase folds case inside the generated query, so all three vendor schemas match identically. Do not rely on H2's VARCHAR_IGNORECASE or MySQL's default collation.

notes:
Narrowest reading recorded for the one open product question (PRD § Open Questions, naming a specialty twice): ?specialty=a&specialty=b binds through Spring's default array-to-String conversion to a comma-joined value, which matches no specialty and yields the normal listing with an empty vet list and HTTP 200. No special handling and no test is contracted for it; the behavior falls out of the framework's binding.

Padded names: the controller strips, per the PRD's recorded reading and OwnerController's precedent. The strip happens before the blank test, so an all-space value is the absent case.

Brief gap, surfaced rather than overridden: security-principles.md § Realization carries no row for composing a request-derived value into a URL. Its cross-site-scripting row covers markup injection and output escaping only. The URL-encoding risk above is recorded in this block because the brief that would own the principle is outside my write scope.

Autofix audit: the handoff log holds no design-doc-autofix records, so the audit is a no-op this dispatch.

Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (Contracts rows, § Persistence, Known Defects row removed), docs/adr/2026-09-06-vet-cache-excludes-filtered-reads.md (new), docs/adr/README.md (index rows for both 2026-09-06 ADRs, including the product expert's non-goal ADR).

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: This slice introduces the first instance in the codebase of a request-derived string composed into a URL the application emits, and the Realization table has no row for that class. The XSS row covers HTML escaping of rendered markup, which is a different control from URL-encoding a query-parameter value: a concatenated href would pass the XSS row while still letting a caller-supplied value inject an extra query parameter into the emitted link. The code here does the right thing (Thymeleaf link expressions with parameters on both branches, verified by the encoding test at VetControllerTests.theVetListPagingShouldEncodeASpecialtyNameCarryingAUrlDelimiter), and the ADR records the decision, but the durable bar the next implementer designs against still has no row. Ask whether the brief should gain one, worded so the control is 'link expression with parameters, never string concatenation'.

recommendations: Supply chain: no NVD matching ran in this review. The project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin, and the change set does not touch build.gradle (Spring Boot 4.1.1 via the plugin, unchanged), so there is no dependency delta to verify. Treat the framework versions as not verified against the NVD in this pass; a CI or human check closes it.

vetList.html line 20 binds a th:each local variable also named 'specialty' (the Specialty entity), while the pagination block below reads the model attribute 'specialty' (the request-derived filter string). The scopes do not overlap today, so there is no defect, but two different values under one name in one template is the shape in which an encoding assumption later changes meaning unnoticed. Renaming the loop variable would remove the ambiguity.

Every filtered request reaches the database, by design. That matches the existing uncached owner-search surface and is strictly better than the unbounded-cache alternative, so it is not a regression against the recorded baseline; it is worth knowing as the accepted trade-off if this application is ever deployed outside the demonstration framing.
approved_aspects: Data access: both new finders are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase), so the caller-supplied name binds as a query parameter. No @Query string, no concatenated JPQL or SQL anywhere in the change. The 'Injection into data access' row passes.

URL composition and XSS: every one of the five pagination links in vetList.html uses the link-expression-with-parameters form on both branches, so the specialty is URL-encoded and then attribute-escaped. The previous __${...}__ preprocessing form was removed rather than extended, which also removes the template-expression-evaluation surface from this file; the specialty never reaches a preprocessed expression. The '&' and blank-value tests pin the encoding behavior.

Class sweep for request-derived values composed into URLs: swept every th:href / th:src / th:action in src/main/resources/templates/. The remaining preprocessing sites (layout.html menu link, ownersList.html and ownerDetails.html paging and id links) interpolate an int page number, an entity id, or a fixed constant, none request-derived as text. vetList.html is the only instance of the class and it is handled correctly.

Cache key space: the omission of @Cacheable on both filtered finders is the right call and is justified in place. Caching them would key the JCache-backed 'vets' cache on caller-supplied text with no eviction bound, which is an unauthenticated memory-growth primitive on a route that needs no credentials. The whole-directory reads keep their existing caching, so the change removes nothing.

Input handling at the boundary: activeSpecialty normalizes null / blank / padded to a single null 'no filter' state before any use, and both surfaces share the one helper, so the HTML and JSON routes cannot diverge on how a hostile value is read.

Exposed surface: no new route. /vets and /vets.html both existed and both already published the full specialty list publicly, so the filter discloses nothing a caller could not already read, and no enumeration oracle is created.

No secrets, no credentials, no logging, no file or process or network I/O, no deserialization configuration, and no serialization annotations in the change. build.gradle is untouched, so the change adds no dependency and no supply-chain delta.

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet list surfaces by specialty

blast_radius.note: One module and three production files: two new derived finders on VetRepository, an optional parameter plus a shared normalizer on VetController, and the five pagination links in vets/vetList.html. No sensitive paths, no new route, no build or config change; the remaining hunks are docs and tests.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, the code does what its size suggests: strip-then-blank-to-null in activeSpecialty, finder selection on null, and paged links that select between a one-parameter and a two-parameter link expression so an unfiltered page keeps the exact links it had.
